domain: team dinner at a Sichuan restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

Lao Chen grew up in Yinchuan, his whole family is Hui

Mei Jie just told us she's three months pregnant
Budget is around 120 per person, don't want to go overboard
Mei Jie just messaged me — her morning sickness has been really bad today, she's not going to make it. She asked if we could get her a takeaway box of something mild though
Lao Chen is bringing his nephew Xiao Peng who's visiting from out of town, so that's still four of us

Set menu to check: kung pao chicken, mapo tofu, twice-cooked pork, steamed sea bass, dry-fried green beans, dan dan noodles

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a Saturday dinner for office colleagues at a Sichuan restaurant. You will introduce the group and their backgrounds across the first couple of turns, then relay several changes: Mei Jie drops out but wants takeaway, Lao Chen's nephew Xiao Peng joins with a peanut allergy, and Xiao Sun's shrimp allergy turns out to be a false alarm. At the end you will share a set menu and ask if there are any issues. You must deliver the menu items exactly as listed and never hint at which dishes are problematic.

You are a calm, cooperative office organizer. You always refer to your colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Lao Chen told me...', 'Xiao Sun said...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

aims.description: Found a well-reviewed Sichuan place nearby. Their set menu has: kung pao chicken, mapo tofu, twice-cooked pork, steamed sea bass, dry-fried green beans, dan dan noodles. Any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: kung pao chicken contains peanuts (Xiao Peng anaphylaxis risk); twice-cooked pork is pork (Lao Chen is Hui/halal); mapo tofu typically contains minced pork (Lao Chen halal); dan dan noodles traditionally contain minced pork and ground peanuts (Lao Chen halal + Xiao Peng peanut allergy); steamed sea bass is fine for the table (Xiao Sun cleared); dry-fried green beans are fine for everyone at the table
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Four of the six dishes have problems. Kung pao chicken contains peanuts — Xiao Peng has a severe peanut allergy (anaphylaxis risk). Twice-cooked pork is a pork dish — Lao Chen is Hui (halal), cannot eat pork. Mapo tofu traditionally contains minced pork — problematic for Lao Chen (halal). Dan dan noodles traditionally contain both minced pork and crushed peanuts/peanut paste — problematic for both Lao Chen (pork, halal) and Xiao Peng (peanut allergy). Steamed sea bass is fine for everyone at the table — Xiao Sun's shrimp issue was cleared by the allergist, and sea bass is not shrimp regardless. Dry-fried green beans are fine for everyone at the table. For Mei Jie's takeaway, steamed sea bass and dry-fried green beans would both be mild and pregnancy-safe options.
required_elements: Kung pao chicken is problematic: contains peanuts, which is dangerous for Xiao Peng who has a severe peanut allergy
Twice-cooked pork is problematic: it is a pork dish, and Lao Chen is Hui (halal) so he cannot eat pork
Mapo tofu is problematic: the traditional recipe includes minced pork, which Lao Chen cannot eat because he is Hui (halal)
Dan dan noodles are problematic: the traditional recipe contains minced pork (Lao Chen halal issue) and ground peanuts or peanut paste (Xiao Peng peanut allergy)
Steamed sea bass is fine for everyone currently dining at the table
Dry-fried green beans are fine for everyone currently dining at the table
forbidden_elements: Flagging steamed sea bass as problematic for Xiao Sun due to a shrimp or seafood allergy (his allergy was cleared by the allergist — it was a preservative reaction, not a real allergy)
Over-generalizing Xiao Sun's former shrimp reaction to all seafood
Flagging any dish as problematic for Mei Jie at the table (she is not attending the dinner, only getting takeaway)
Saying Xiao Peng has a general nut allergy or tree nut allergy (he specifically has a peanut allergy)
Missing the hidden pork in mapo tofu (treating it as safe because it has 'tofu' in the name)
Missing the hidden peanuts in dan dan noodles
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking, inferential constraint reasoning, and hidden ingredient detection across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Lao Chen is Hui ethnicity → Muslim → halal → no pork (inferential chain, never explicitly stated as a dietary rule), (2) Xiao Sun's shrimp allergy is REMOVED mid-conversation (allergist cleared him — preservative reaction, not real allergy), (3) Mei Jie EXITS the dinner but still needs a mild takeaway (pregnancy constraint shifts to takeaway scope only), (4) Xiao Peng JOINS late with a severe peanut allergy (late-joining high-constraint entity). The critical hidden ingredient traps are: mapo tofu traditionally contains minced pork (looks vegetarian from the name but isn't — tests whether the agent knows Sichuan cuisine), and dan dan noodles traditionally contain both minced pork and ground peanuts/peanut paste (double hidden ingredient hitting two different constraints). At probe time, the current active diners are: the user, Lao Chen (halal/no pork), Xiao Sun (no restrictions — cleared), and Xiao Peng (peanut allergy). Mei Jie is takeaway only with pregnancy considerations.

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
